current.text: He is Detroit's projected starting power forward. He replaces Tobias Harris in a starting five of Cunningham, Robinson, Thompson, Collins and Duren.
He should play 30 to 31 minutes, as Tobias Harris did, because Detroit's power forward depth is weak.
If Ron Holland develops a shot, he could cut into Collins's minutes.
He becomes a category-league value if he plays 31 minutes.
Experts see him as a value around picks 115 to 130 and call him too expensive in the 90s. One expert drafted him around round 10 and calls rounds 9 to 10 fine in category leagues.
Experts see little upside. He is not a 20 and 10 player anymore and will not reach his prime level, though he should beat his rank of about 120 from last season.
Experts see him as a worse real-life fit for Detroit than Tobias Harris, because the team lost Harris's shot creation.
One expert says his drop in free throw shooting to 77% had no clear reason. The same expert says five rebounds in 27 minutes is below his usual level of about eight rebounds.
Experts disagree on his rebounding. One calls him a modest rebounder at about five a game. Another says he is usually about an eight-rebound player.
Detroit plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs, and no rest risk is expected.

durable.text: He is an off-ball play finisher who does not create his own shot. He spaces the corners and cuts.
He has been a good offensive rebounder throughout his career.
His FG% is high, but on modest volume. His FT% is good for a big man. Experts call him a passive player.
He shoots a good percentage from three but takes few threes, and his three-point shooting is streaky.
He does not pass, and assists are his weakest category.
He is a weak defender, and his defensive stats have dropped.

note: Both sites rank him near 96 and value him at only 3 to 4 USD (average cost under 2 USD), and he went for 7 USD in our league last season. That makes him a cheap late frontcourt pick for FG%, rebounds and some blocks, without hurting FT%. Experts value him around picks 115 to 130 with little upside, so do not pay more than a few dollars. Early in the season, check whether he really plays 30 to 31 minutes and gets back toward eight rebounds, and watch whether Ron Holland takes some of his minutes.
